name: SKP
rootCause: The SKP token exposes ownerBurnLiquidityPairTokens(uint256), an owner-only backdoor that burns SKP held directly inside the SKP/USDT PancakeSwap LP pair. The deployer/owner-attacker first burns the bulk (~95%) of the SKP sitting in the pair, then calls sync() on the pair to force the reserves to match the now-depleted SKP balance. Because the USDT reserve is untouched while the SKP reserve is slashed, the on-chain SKP/USDT price spikes (~20x). The owner-attacker then supplies the over-valued SKP as collateral on Venus/Lista DAO and borrows out BTCB + USDT (~$212K). This is a privileged-backdoor + oracle/price-manipulation incident: the token contract should never have been able to burn assets out of an external LP pair on the owner's command. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0xbc01ea37bd2ff8f6aa6afcfbe0406114ff27a01e9aa56102bfa4ad8a0c2f25ee Analysis: DeFiHackLabs PoC

descriptions.text: Owner Backdoor LP Burn + Price Manipulation. Lost: ~$212K USD

The SKP token exposes ownerBurnLiquidityPairTokens(uint256), an owner-only backdoor that burns SKP held directly inside the SKP/USDT PancakeSwap LP pair. The deployer/owner-attacker first burns the bulk (~95%) of the SKP sitting in the pair, then calls sync() on the pair to force the reserves to match the now-depleted SKP balance. Because the USDT reserve is untouched while the SKP reserve is slashed, the on-chain SKP/USDT price spikes (~20x). The owner-attacker then supplies the over-valued SKP as collateral on Venus/Lista DAO and borrows out BTCB + USDT (~$212K). This is a privileged-backdoor + oracle/price-manipulation incident: the token contract should never have been able to burn assets out of an external LP pair on the owner's command. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0xbc01ea37bd2ff8f6aa6afcfbe0406114ff27a01e9aa56102bfa4ad8a0c2f25ee Analysis: DeFiHackLabs PoC

On BSC, the SKP token suffered a token-side LP balance drain + sync attack. The attacker profited approximately $212.85k in a single transaction (162,854.21 USDT + 75.88 BNB). The root cause was a flaw in SKP token logic that allowed extra SKP tokens to be transferred out from the Pancake V2 SKP/USDT LP after a large buy, followed by calling sync() to write incorrect reserves, pushing the SKP reserve close to zero. The attacker used flash loans to amplify the attack.

On May 26, 2026, SKP on BNB Chain suffered a $212,000 exploit driven by a malicious transfer-hook that forced AMM reserve sync during trades. The attacker drained nearly all USDT from the PancakeSwap pair by manipulating reserves mid-transaction. The SKP token included a custom transfer-hook that conditionally called sync() on its PancakeSwap USDT pair during token transfers. This allowed the attacker to collapse the SKP reserve mid-swap, making USDT extraction possible. The hook was deliberately added in SKP's contract design, triggered via privileged whitelisting.
